```{r setup}
library(housepi)

```

# Infectivity profiles in housepi

In `housepi` we follow the convention for infectivity profiles to be function of the generation time.
Generation time is defined as the time from infection to transmission.

Certain profiles will then be conditioned on individuals incubation periods

| Delay                 | Infector Incub. Period | Infectee Incub. Period | Supported |
|-----------------------|:----------------------:|:----------------------:|:---------:|
| Generation Time       | &cross;                | &cross;                |  &check;  |
| Onset to Transmission | &check;                | &cross;                |  &check;  |
| Serial Time           | &check;                | &check;                |  &cross;  |

Imagine we would like to associate a gamma distribution as infectivity profile.
In this simple hypothesis all individuals will share the same profile which depends only on the generation time.
We can provide a custom infectivity profile calling `add_infec_profile()` as follows:

```{r}
hhsimul <- new_housepi_model("augmented_infection_time") |>
  load_parameter_template() |>
  add_infec_profile(name = "gamma", args = c(shape = 2.2, scale = 1.3))
```

Bear in mind that each model requiring an infectivity profile has a default profile.

# Other custom functions (advanced)

Custom functions are added in the C++ source code by inheriting from a base class
`Function`, and overriding one or more of their virtual methods.

Once our function class is defined, we can register it using the macro `REGISTER_USER_FUNCTION`, making the new function available to the model system and to R by its register name.

In our simplified example, we define a custom "monomial" function. 
This is done by providing a constructor with the register name, its argument names and default valued, and by overriding the `raw_call_` method as follows 
```{Rcpp, eval=FALSE}
// inside path/to/mymodel/
class MyMonomialFunction : public Function {
public:
    MyMonomialFunction()          // constructor
        : Function("my_monomial", // function name used in registers
                   {"a", "b"},    // names of arguments
                   {1.0, 1.0},    // default values
                   0.0) {}        // value of the minimum
  
protected:
    // internal method called when the function is evaluated
    double raw_call_(double x) const override final {
        const double a = arg(0); // arguments order is by definition
        const double b = arg(1);
        return a * std::pow(x, b);
    }
};

// register user function so that it can be used in the analysis
REGISTER_USER_FUNCTION(CustomSquareFunction)
```

## How It Works
\item Inheritance and Constructor:
The class `MyMonomialFunction` inherits from `Function`. 
In the constructor, we define:
\item The register name of the function;
\item A list of argument names (note that "x" is reserved);
\item A list of default argument values;
\item Information about minimum and maximum value.

\item Overriding methods:
The `raw_call_` method is overridden to implement the core computation. 

\item Macro Registration:
The `REGISTER_USER_FUNCTION` macro at the end registers the custom function. 
This makes the "my_monomial" function available to the framework and allows you to associate directly from R.

Once generate the new model, the function will be visible from its environment and you will be able to test it as follows

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| include: true
hhmodel <- new_housepi_model("path/to/mymodel/")
x <- seq(0, 5, 0.5)
test_function("my_monomial", x, args = c(a = 2, b = 3), model = hhmodel)
```

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| include: false
x <- seq(0, 5, 0.5)
a <- 2
b <- 3
cat(a * x ^ b)
```

## Discretization, distributions

Optionally, we can enable discretization by overriding `init_discretization` and providing a primitive (cumulative function) via `raw_primitive_`. 
This is useful if your function is later integrated or used in a discretized setting.

\item Providing a primitive:
Implement `raw_primitive_` if you need a cumulative version of your function (or another primitive), for example when integrating the function over time.
\item Initialize reshaping:
If discretization is needed, override `init_discretization`. In our case, we call the helper `init_discr_helper_` with a flag (e. g. `HSP_DISCR_LEFT`) to tell the framework that our function should be rearranged according to a given discretization scheme (e. g. left discretization). 
If it's not discrete defined (flag `HSP_DISCR_DEFINED`), a primitive must be provided.

```{Rcpp, eval=FALSE}
class MyCustomFunction : public Function {
public:
    // constructor...
    
    // enable left discretization
    void init_discretization() { init_discr_helper_(HSP_DISCR_LEFT); } 

protected:
    //  raw_call_ ...
    
    // internal method called when the function is evaluated
    double raw_primitive_(double x) const override final {
        const double a = arg(0), b_plus_1 = arg(1) + 1;
        return a * std::pow(x, b_plus_1) / (b_plus_1);
    }
};
```
